_meta.description: BIS hallmarking of precious metal articles: which products it covers, whether it is compulsory, and the order that makes it so. Read by hand from the gazette notifications BIS publishes, saved in source/hallmarking/.

documents.read: S.O. 205(E), 15 January 2020, in force 15 January 2021: gold jewellery and gold artefacts shall conform to IS 1417:2016 (as amended) and bear the hallmark, sold only by registered jewellers. Exemptions (a) to (g): export to a foreign buyer's specification, articles under 2 g, consignments to a hallmarking centre, medical, dental, veterinary, scientific or industrial use, gold thread, articles not substantially complete, and gold bullion in any shape (bar, plate, sheet, foil, rod, wire, strip, tube or coin).

S.O. 2481(E), 23 June 2021: the order applies only to the districts in its Annexure. Exemptions (h) to (m) added: export and re-import, international exhibitions, government-approved business-to-business exhibitions, Kundan, Polki and Jadau jewellery, watches and fountain pens, and jewellers with annual turnover up to Rs 40 lakh.
S.O. 1594(E), 4 April 2022, in force 1 June 2022: the limit to 14, 18 and 22 carat is omitted, so every caratage IS 1417 permits is covered.

S.O. 1047(E), 6 March 2023: after 31 March 2023 no person shall sell, display or offer to sell gold jewellery or gold artefacts unless hallmarked to IS 1417:2016 as amended in July 2021 (the amendment that introduced HUID).
S.O. 4345(E), Third Amendment Order 2026, 3 August 2026: substitutes the Annexure of districts. The principal order was last amended before it by S.O. 2117(E), 28 April 2026.
BIS, September 2026: 256 districts in the first phase and 32, 55, 18, 12, 7, 5 and 7 added in phases two to eight, 392 districts in all.
BIS guidelines on the exemptions, including definitions of Kundan, Polki and Jadau jewellery.

BIS FAQ: gold and silver are under hallmarking. IS 1417 permits 14K (585), 18K (750), 20K (833), 22K (916), 23K (958) and 24K (995); IS 2112 permits silver of 800, 835, 900, 925, 970 and 990 fineness. The hallmark is the BIS logo, the purity in carat and fineness, and a six-digit alphanumeric HUID.

_meta.note: Only gold is under the compulsory order; silver hallmarking under IS 2112 is available but voluntary. status 'voluntary' means a BIS scheme exists for the product but no order makes it compulsory.

entries.gazette: S.O. 205(E), 15 January 2020, as amended, last by S.O. 4345(E), 3 August 2026
entries.conditions: Compulsory in the 392 districts listed in the order (Annexure as substituted on 3 August 2026): gold jewellery and artefacts may not be sold there unless hallmarked to IS 1417, which the hallmark shows as the BIS logo, the purity in carat and fineness, and a six-digit HUID. The order exempts, among others, articles under 2 g, gold bullion (bars, coins and similar), gold thread, articles for export, Kundan, Polki and Jadau jewellery, watches and fountain pens, and jewellers with an annual turnover up to Rs 40 lakh.

entries.conditions: IS 2112 permits hallmarking at 800, 835, 900, 925, 970 and 990 fineness.
